εὐ-άρεστος, -ον well-pleasing, acceptable: [[r:ROM.12.2|Rom 12:2]]; with dative of person(s), [[r:ROM.12.1|Rom 12:1 14:16]], [[r:2CO.5.9|2Co 5:9]], [[r:EPH.5.10|Eph 5:10]], [[r:PHP.4.18|Php 4:18]]; id. before ἐν, [[r:TIT.2.9|Tit 2:9]] (κυρίῳ), [[r:COL.3.20|Col 3:20]]; ἐνώπιον, [[r:HEB.13.21|Heb 13:21]] (for ex. in Inser., see Deiss., BS, 215).† (AS)

G2104.strongs: well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous

G2105.strongs: a clear sky, i.e. fine weather

(Polyb., al.), to be well pleased, to think it good, to give consent (so frequently in π. in legal docu­ments; Milligan, Th., 22 f.): [[r:LUK.12.32|Luk 12:32]], [[r:ROM.15.26|Rom 15:26-27]], [[r:1CO.1.21|1Co 1:21]], [[r:GAL.1.15|Gal 1:15]], [[r:COL.1.19|Col 1:19]], R, mg. (ICC, in l, but see infr.), [[r:1TH.2.8|1Th 2:8 3:1]]; μᾶλλον εὐ., [[r:2CO.5.8|2Co 5:8]]; with accusative and inf. (Polyb., i, 8, 4), Col, l.with, R, txt. (Lft., in l).
to be well pleased or take pleasure with or in a person or thing;

as frequently in LXX, α with accusative: [[r:MAT.12.13|Mat 12:13]], [[r:HEB.10.5|Heb 10:5]], 8" (LXX); β before ἐν (cf. Heb. בּ רָצָה, [[r:PSA.149.4|Psa 149:4]]): [[r:MAT.3.17|Mat 3:17 17:5]], [[r:MRK.1.11|Mrk 1:11]], [[r:LUK.3.22|Luk 3:22]] (on the tense, see M, Pr., 134 f.; DCG, i,308 b), [[r:1CO.10.5|1Co 10:5]], [[r:2CO.12.10|2Co 12:10]], [[r:HEB.10.38|Heb 10:38]]" (LXX); (with) before εἰς: [[r:2PE.1.17|2Pe 1:17.]] (cf. συν-ευδοκέω, and see Cremer, 213 f.; Field, Notes, 48 f.; DCG, i, 355a.)† (AS)

senses: (εὐδοκέω, which see), good pleasure, good-will, satisfaction, approval: [[r:MAT.11.26|Mat 11:26]], [[r:LUK.10.21|Luk 10:21]], [[r:ROM.10.1|Rom 10:1]], [[r:EPH.1.5|Eph 1:5]], 9, [[r:PHP.1.15|Php 1:15 2:13]]; with genitive obj., [[r:2TH.1.11|2Th 1:11]] (see Milligan, in l); ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία, Rec., R, mg., WH, mg. (see Field, Notes, 48 f.), [[r:LUK.2.14|Luk 2:14]]; -ας, Lk, l.with, R, txt., WH, txt. (see ICC, in l; WH, App., in l).† (AS)
(εὐεργέτης), a good deed, kindness, benefit: [[r:1TI.6.2|1Ti 6:2]]; with genitive of person(s) (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b), [[r:ACT.4.9|Act 4:9]],† (AS)

G2110.strongs: a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist

G2113.strongs: to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct
senses: of ships, to run a straight course (Philo): [[r:ACT.16.11|Act 16:11 21:1]].† (AS)

G2114.strongs: to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully
senses: Intrans. (Eur., Plut.; so mid. in Xen., Plat.), to be of good cheer: [[r:ACT.27.22|Act 27:22, 25]], [[r:JAS.5.13|Jas 5:13]].† (AS)

G2115.kjv: of good cheer, the more cheerfully

G2117.strongs: straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once
G2117.kjv: anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway
senses: straight, direct: τρίβοι, [[r:MAT.3.3|Mat 3:3]], [[r:MRK.1.3|Mrk 1:3]], [[r:LUK.3.4|Luk 3:4]]" (LXX); εἰς εὐθειας, (sc. ὁδούς), [[r:LUK.3.5|Luk 3:5]]; εὐ. ὐδός, figuratively, [[r:ACT.13.10|Act 13:10]], [[r:2PE.2.15|2Pe 2:15]]; as (Proper name) of a street, [[r:ACT.9.11|Act 9:11.]]

G2119.strongs: to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure
senses: (= cl., εὖ σχολῆς ἔχειν; used by Polyb. and Philo; cf. Rutherford, NPhr. 205; MM, Exp., xiv), to have leisure or opportunity: [[r:1CO.16.12|1Co 16:12]]; with inf., [[r:MRK.6.31|Mrk 6:31]]; before εἰς, to devote one's leisure to, [[r:ACT.17.21|Act 17:21.]]† (AS)

εὔ-καιρος, -ον timely, seasonable, suitable (Cremer, 740): ἡμέρα, [[r:MRK.6.21|Mrk 6:21]] (or empty, as in Byz. and MGr.; see MM, Exp., xiv); βοήθεια, [[r:HEB.4.16|Heb 4:16.]]† (AS)
εὐκαίρως adv., seasonably, in season: [[r:MRK.14.11|Mrk 14:11]]; opposite to ἀκ- (Kühner3, iv, 346 d), [[r:2TI.4.2|2Ti 4:2.]]† (AS)

G2124.strongs: properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely)

senses: to be cautious, to beware: [[r:ACT.23.10|Act 23:10]] (Rec.; φοβηθείς, WH, RV).

G2127.strongs: to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper)

[[r:ISA.61.9|Isa 61:9]]), [[r:MAT.25.34|Mat 25:34]]; pass. [[r:ACT.3.25|Act 3:25]] (cf. ἐν-, κατ-ευλογέω).† SYN.: see: αἰνέω, and cf. DCG, i, 189, 211; Cremer, 766 (AS)

Metaphorical, to find, find out by inquiry, learn, discover: [[r:LUK.19.48|Luk 19:48]], [[r:ACT.4.21|Act 4:21]]; αἰτίαν, [[r:JHN.18.38|Jhn 18:38]], [[r:ACT.13.28|Act 13:28]], al.; pass., [[r:MAT.1.18|Mat 1:18]], [[r:LUK.17.18|Luk 17:18]], [[r:ROM.7.10|Rom 7:10]], [[r:1CO.4.2|1Co 4:2]], [[r:GAL.2.17|Gal 2:17]], [[r:1PE.1.7|1Pe 1:7]], [[r:REV.5.4|Rev 5:4]], al.; of attaining to the knowledge of God, εὑ. θεόν, [[r:ACT.17.27|Act 17:27]]; pass., [[r:ROM.10.20|Rom 10:20]] (LXX). G2151.strongs: to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support)

(εὖ, σέβομαι), pious, godly, devout: [[r:ACT.10.2|Act 10:2]], 7, [[r:2PE.2.9|2Pe 2:9]].† SYN.: θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (see Tr., Syn., § xlviii; DB, ii, 221 f.; Cremer, 524 f., 858) (AS)
in Hippocr., as medical term (LS, see word).

G2159.strongs: in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely)

G2160.strongs: witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry
senses: = βωμολογία, coarse jesting, ribaldry (Abbott, Essays, 93): [[r:EPH.5.4|Eph 5:4.]]† SYN.: μωρολογία, see Tr., Syn., § xxxiv (AS)

G2161.strongs: well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man

senses: (εὖ, φήμη), primarily, utter­ing words or sounds of good omen, hence,

senses: εὐφραίνω to cheer, gladden: with accusative of person(s), opposite to λυπεῖν, [[r:2CO.2.2|2Co 2:2.]] Pass., to be happy, rejoice, make merry: [[r:LUK.15.32|Luk 15:32]], [[r:ACT.2.26|Act 2:26]]" (LXX) [[r:ROM.15.10|Rom 15:10]] (LXX), [[r:GAL.4.27|Gal 4:27]] (LXX), [[r:REV.11.10|Rev 11:10 12:12]]; before ἐν, [[r:ACT.7.41|Act 7:41]]; ἐπί with dative, [[r:REV.18.20|Rev 18:20]]; of merry-making at a feast ([[r:1KI.4.20|3Ki 4:20]]; of. Milligan, Th., 5; Ellic. on [[r:COL.1.12|Col 1:12]]; Lft., Notes, 9): [[r:ROM.1.21|Rom 1:21]], [[r:1CO.14.17|1Co 14:17]], [[r:1TH.5.18|1Th 5:18]]; of giving thanks before meat, [[r:MAT.15.36|Mat 15:36 26:27]], [[r:MRK.8.6|Mrk 8:6 14:23]], [[r:LUK.22.17|Luk 22:17, 19]], [[r:JHN.6.11|Jhn 6:11, 23]], [[r:1CO.11.24|1Co 11:24]]; with dative pens., τ. θεῷ, [[r:LUK.17.16|Luk 17:16]], [[r:ACT.27.35|Act 27:35 28:15]], [[r:ROM.14.6|Rom 14:6 16:4]], [[r:1CO.14.18|1Co 14:18]], [[r:PHP.1.3|Php 1:3]], [[r:COL.1.3|Col 1:3, 12]], Phm 4; before διὰ Ἰ.
